title: Per-endpoint SLI taxonomy, error-budget burn actions, and multi-region failover orchestration
creator: Priya Shah
description: Define a single, consistent SLI/SLO taxonomy and operational policy for model endpoints (per-model and per-route), plus the error-budget burn actions and an automated multi-region failover/circuit-breaker choreography. Goal: enable predictable observability and automated mitigations without manual intervention for common infra and model degradations.
background: We currently have ad-hoc SLOs across teams and no standard runbook that links SLI measurement -> error budget tracking -> automated mitigation (circuit breaker, load shed, failover). That has led to inconsistent alerts, unexpected rollouts during incidents, and manual firefighting. This ticket produces the definition and automation spec required by Console, Serving runtime, and Ops teams.
proposed_sli_definitions:
High-level SLI categories (applies to text-generation, chat-streaming, embeddings, rerank):
- Latency SLI: edge-to-first-token P50/P95/P99 measured at API gateway with synthetic and real traffic tags. Exclude requests that are aborted by client within 100ms and known long-context jobs tagged as 'batch'.
- Availability SLI: successful-response rate measured as HTTP 2xx with model-level success (no model-runtime 5xx and no partial-token failures) over rolling 30d and 7d windows.
- Correctness SLI (quality): periodic eval-based regression metric per-model (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) reported daily and tied to release gating.
- Throughput SLI: sustained token/sec per instance compared to provisioned capacity to detect saturation.
Sample per-tier SLO targets (example):
- Hosted-standard: Latency P99 <= 300ms 99.9% of the hour, Availability >= 99.95% 30d.
- Dedicated-enterprise: Latency P99 <= 250ms 99.95% of the hour, Availability >= 99.99% 30d.
- Private-onprem: baseline SLOs are contractual; platform will surface measured SLIs but not auto-enforce cross-tenant actions without customer opt-in.
error_budget_policy:
Define error budget as 1 - availability SLO over a rolling 30d window. Burn policy (escalation steps):
- Green (<= 25% budget used in 30d): normal ops.
- Watch (25% - 50%): ops notified, pause non-critical platform rollouts for affected region & model.
- Alert (50% - 80%): auto-throttle low-tier customers on affected route, route new traffic to fallback model variants, mark release hold.
- Critical (>80%): initiate multi-region failover according to failover_playbook, escalate to oncall P1, and trigger emergency autoscaling (if available).
Fast-burn detection: if >40% of budget burned in 24h -> immediate Watch/Alert actions depending on absolute remaining budget.
Budget accounting: per-endpoint, per-model and aggregated per-customer. Console must show live burn rate and projected exhaustion time.
failover_playbook:
Multi-region orchestration guidelines (automated + manual):
1) Trigger conditions: persistent SLI breach (Availability < SLO for 10m) OR critical error-budget (>80% burned) OR regional capacity alarm.
2) Pre-flight checks (automated): confirm region health metric aggregate, check compatible model variants in target region, verify data residency policy for customer.
3) Automated actions: open circuit breaker for affected region-route, start traffic mirroring to target region, then gradually shift traffic using weighted routing (10/30/60/100 over 5m steps) with health probes.
4) Rollback: automatic rollback if P95 latency or error rate in target region exceeds origin by >2x during any step; manual override available for SRE.
5) Postmortem: tag events with runbook ID, capture timing of triage, traffic shifts, and final root cause attribution.
Notes: failover must preserve model variant compatibility and API contract. For dedicated customers, failover requires customer opt-in unless contractual language permits automatic region fallback.
circuit_breakers_and_load_shedding_spec:
Circuit breaker triggers (examples):
- Error-rate CB: 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 5m for endpoints with >100rps baseline.
- Latency CB: P99 latency > 4x latency SLO for 3m.
- Resource CB: per-GPU token queue length > 80% of safe limit for 60s.
CB actions:
- Soft trip: mark endpoint as degraded, route new low-priority traffic to fallback model, enable aggressive batching and prefix caching.
- Hard trip: return 503 with structured JSON explaining degradation and Retry-After header; automatically fall back to pre-configured smaller model or regional replica.
Load-shedding priorities: 1) admin/system checks (highest), 2) enterprise/dedicated customers, 3) standard paying customers, 4) trial/free usage (lowest).
Shedding mechanisms: token-cap per-request, early-reject for extremely long contexts, delay streaming commits into smaller chunks for heavy requests.
Circuit-breaker observability: every trip must emit an event with trip_reason, affected_model, region, and active_action so Console can present timelines and correlate to error budget burn.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards and alerts required:
- Per-endpoint SLI dashboard (P50/P95/P99 latency, success rate, error budget burn rate, traffic volume).
- Error-budget alerting: watch/alert/critical thresholds with actionable runbook links.
- Failover run metrics: traffic weights, health probe success ratio, step timings.
- CB events timeline: frequency and duration of soft/hard trips per model.
Alert destinations: Slack #sre-alerts, PagerDuty for critical (>80% burn) and auto-failover failures. Console must expose SLI history and annotate deployments, PRs, and runbooks.
rollout_plan:
Deliverables and milestones:
- Week 1: finalize SLI taxonomy and sample SLO targets, review with PM and Product Security.
- Week 2: instrument uniform SLI metrics in runtime (gateway + service) and add labels for model, route, customer-tier.
- Week 3: implement error-budget tracker service and integrate with Console.
- Week 4: implement simple CB automation in staging + simulated failover tests.
- Week 5: run chaos/failure drills, adjust thresholds, publish runbook and perform oncall training.
- Week 6: ship to prod behind a feature flag and monitor burn for two weeks before removing flag.
Acceptance criteria are listed separately.
open_questions:
- How do we reconcile model-quality SLI regressions across model families when the SLO is expressed in different metrics?
- Do we expose automatic cross-region failover for Private deployments by default, or require opt-in?
- What is the canonical source of per-customer tiering used by the CB and shedding logic (billing metadata or auth token)?
- Should error budget accounting include partial responses (e.g., truncated streams) as full failures or a separate failure bucket?
acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI definitions documented and reviewed by PM, Design, and Applied ML
Instrumentation merged in runtime and gateway with tags: model_id, route, customer_tier
Error-budget UI in Console shows live burn rate and forecast for at least 5 models
Automated circuit-breaker actions implemented in staging with deterministic tests
Multi-region failover automation executed successfully in two simulated incidents and rollback works
Runbooks published and oncall trained; post-drill retrospective captured
